messages:
maria: FYI seeing sustained saturation on the inference fleet in us-west-2 for the last 10m, tail latency climbing and a bunch of 503s from the proxy.
jeff: On it. Is this the usual nightly batch or something spiky from customer X?
samir: Not batch. traffic from multiple orgs stepped up. GPUs fully busy, requests are queuing at the admission controller.
ingrid: Do we currently enforce token-bucket per-org or just per-key global? I thought we had org pools in the new design.
maria: Running per-key buckets upstream and a crude global burst cap at proxy. No org-level pool enforcement in the proxy yet.
luis: That explains unfairness — big orgs are stealing bursts. We need capacity-tied limits so per-org rate ≈ fraction_of_pool_capacity * k.
jeff: Agreed. Proposal: admission controller maintains per-org token-bucket where refill rate is derived from org's reserved GPU share + recent usage smoothing.
samir: Also add a small leaky-buffer queue for short bursts, then reject with 429 when queue + tokens exhausted. Keeps latency bounded.
ingrid: Sketch config (pseudo):

```
org_pools:
  org_id: "acme"
  reserved_gpu_share: 0.12
  refill_rate_tokens_per_sec: 120 # derived from model QPS & reserved_share
  burst_capacity_tokens: 600
  queue_ms: 200
```

maria: How do we compute tokens -> GPU cycles? We need a stable unit across models and sequence lengths.
luis: Use estimated tokens-per-gpu-second per model family (measured). admission converts requested work to GPU-seconds, then token bucket tracks GPU-seconds not raw requests.
jeff: Nice. That gets cost-awareness in the admission path. Also need fallback rules: if org hits limit, try route to cheaper quantized variant or lower-quality model instead of outright reject.
samir: Fallbacks sound good but need SLA tags. Some orgs pay for guaranteed latency — must bypass fallbacks or consume reserved pool.
ingrid: For safety, add circuit-breaker on pool-level to stop accepting new canary rollouts when overall GPU occupancy > 92%.
ops-bot: Incident alert created: #INC-2456 - us-west-2 inference saturation. Pager notified.
maria: Implementation notes:
- admission component stores per-org state in memory with periodic persistence to etcd
- refill policy uses EWMA of cluster capacity to handle node flaps
- metrics: per-org tokens_used, rejects, fallback_routed_count, avg_queue_ms
- admin API to bump reserved_share for enterprise customers

jeff: Cost side: throttling to reserved_share reduces overage spend, but routing to cheaper models might increase downstream eval/regressions. Need feature flag rollout.
luis: Can we simulate with traffic replay in staging? Run a 2x load test and validate fair shares and fallbacks.
maria: I'll put a design doc and a short PoC task. For now, quick mitigation: temporarily reduce proxy global burst cap and enable early rejects for non-enterprise orgs.
samir: +1, do it now. I'll monitor evictions and queue lengths.
ingrid: Thanks team. Follow-up in eng-infra ASYNC thread with design doc link. :thumbsup:"
